source.title_on_document: Framing an AI with Values Reduces AI Reliance in AI-supported Writing Tasks

supplement.holds: Study surveys and writing prompts; participant demographics (Table 6, p. 24); full writing-outcome means, SDs and t-tests (Tables 10–11, p. 26); additional ANOVA tests and classification of AI suggestions.

paper_design_summary: One between-subjects online study analyzed 149 Prolific participants from India and the United States, each completing two writing tasks with GPT-4o autocomplete under one of four conditions varying the presence, timing and comparative framing of an AI-values overview (PDF pp. 4–6, Methods). The text does not explain allocation to these conditions; explicit random selection concerns writing prompts (p. 6, §3.4.2; p. 23, Table 4). Final essays were assessed with within-essay type-token ratios, similarity across different participants’ same-topic essays, and thematic analysis, alongside measures of AI reliance (pp. 7–8, §3.5; pp. 11–12, §4.3.1).

assignment.what_was_assigned: Four between-participant intervention conditions: No Intervention, AI Values, Primed + AI Values, and Primed + Comparative AI Values. All participants received GPT-4o writing suggestions. The condition-allocation mechanism is not stated, so no assignment-mechanism sentence is available to quote; random selection of writing prompts does not establish random allocation of these intervention conditions.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4, §3 Methods and Table 1; p. 5, §§3.2–3.3; p. 6, §3.4.2; p. 23, Appendix A.2.2, Table 4. Full text and Appendices A–E checked for condition allocation.

arms.name: No Intervention
arms.description: Baseline: values survey before writing, with GPT-4o autocomplete but no AI-values overview (PDF p. 4, Table 1). Analyzed count: p. 5, §3.2.

arms.name: AI Values
arms.description: Non-comparative AI-values overview before the writing tasks; participants complete their own values survey after writing (PDF p. 4, Table 1). Analyzed count: p. 5, §3.2.

arms.name: Primed + AI Values
arms.description: Participants complete their own values survey, then see the non-comparative AI-values overview before writing (PDF p. 4, Table 1). Analyzed count: p. 5, §3.2.

arms.name: Primed + Comparative AI Values
arms.description: Participants complete their own values survey, then see their values compared with the framed AI values before writing (PDF p. 4, Table 1). Analyzed count: p. 5, §3.2.

participants.exclusions: Only participants with valid writing responses were analyzed; responses were invalid if they did not answer the correct writing prompts. The actual recruited/assigned total and the number excluded are not reported. The recruitment target is not an observed enrollment count (PDF p. 5, §3.2 Recruitment & Participants).
participants.who: English-fluent Prolific participants over 18, recruited in the United States or India and reporting no more than 6 months living abroad; analyzed sample comprised 76 American and 73 Indian participants with valid writing responses.
participants.quote: In total, we had 149 participants with valid responses: 40 participants formed the baseline group, 39 participants in AI values condition, 34 participants in primed + AI values condition, and 36 participants in comparative condition.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5, §3.2 Recruitment & Participants; p. 24, Appendix B, Table 6. Counts refer to valid responses analyzed, not a reported randomized sample.

ai_tool.how_used: All arms used autocomplete suggestions conditioned on the essay topic and current text. Suggestions appeared as gray ghost text, were limited to 10 words and retrieved every 500ms; participants accepted with Tab or ignored by continuing to type (PDF p. 6, §3.4.2). The interventions varied the framing of AI values before use.

task.description: Two sequential writing tasks with a minimum of 50 words each: the first randomly chosen between favorite food and favorite festival/holiday, and the second randomly chosen between favorite celebrity/public figure and an email requesting leave from a boss (PDF p. 5, §3.3; p. 6, §3.4.2; p. 23, Table 4).

outcomes.name: Cosine similarity between different participants’ same-topic essays within condition
outcomes.question: across_people

contrasts.reported: AI Values: M = 0.462, SD = 0.129; No Intervention: M = 0.531, SD = 0.161; t(1575.13) = −10.008, p < .0001, d = −0.477, 95% CI [−∞, −0.057]. Lower cosine similarity denotes greater between-person diversity; the reported signs are retained. The methods describe same-topic essay-pair similarities averaged to a participant score, but the reported test degrees of freedom are inconsistent with participant-level analysis. The inferential unit cannot be confirmed and is left null.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 10, §4.3; p. 26, Tables 10–11; pp. 7–8, §3.5.2 for pairwise computation and stated participant averaging.

diversity_detail.metric: Cosine similarity between essay embeddings; lower similarity indicates greater between-person diversity.
diversity_detail.embedding_model: OpenAI text-embedding-large (exact model label printed in PDF p. 7, §3.5.2).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Each participant’s essays were compared with all other participants’ same-topic essays within the same condition. The methods state that the scores for each participant’s two essays were averaged into a final similarity score (PDF pp. 7–8, §3.5.2 Writing Uniqueness).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Bonferroni-corrected one-tailed t-tests comparing intervention conditions with baseline and the comparative condition with the non-comparative conditions (PDF p. 10, §4.3; p. 26, Table 11). The unit used in the reported tests cannot be confirmed.
diversity_detail.notes: The reported test degrees of freedom do not reconcile with participant-level inference despite the methods’ description of participant averaging; unit and n_units remain null. The reported signs are on the similarity scale and are retained (PDF pp. 7–8, §3.5.2; p. 10, §4.3; p. 26, Table 11).

contrasts.reported: AI Values: M = 0.771, SD = 0.071; No Intervention: M = 0.782, SD = 0.057; t(147.64) = −1.075, p = 0.086 (as printed in Table 11). The paper reports no significant increase in lexical diversity. This measure counts unique words relative to total words within an essay, rather than comparing different people’s outputs.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 26, Tables 10–11; p. 10, §4.3; p. 7, §3.5.2 for the type-token-ratio definition.

outcomes.name: Essay-coded uniqueness/personal detail (descriptive response percentages)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Thematic coding of essay uniqueness through personal anecdotes or specified reasons. The first author coded essays within each topic, using a codebook and themes refined with the other authors. This is a descriptive indicator of personal specificity, not a rated overall-creativity score. Percentages are reported relative to the total number of responses per writing task; the corresponding observation counts are not printed (PDF pp. 11–12, §4.3.1 Thematic Analysis on Essays).

contrasts.reported: Essay-coded uniqueness/personal detail: AI Values 60.3%; No Intervention 38.8%. These are descriptive response percentages. The paper states that percentages are relative to responses per writing task; corresponding observation counts, a test statistic and an interval are not reported for this comparison. Direction records the descriptive difference only.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 12, §4.3.1, Uniqueness only when requested; pp. 11–12 for coding and percentage-denominator description.

eligibility.reason: The paper calls the study a controlled, between-subjects online experiment but does not state how participants entered the intervention arms (PDF pp. 4–6, §§3–3.4.2; complete text and Appendices A–E checked). The randomization explicitly described is selection of writing prompts, not allocation of AI-framing conditions (p. 23, Table 4), so criterion 1 is unclear and design_class is other rather than a confirmed randomized or non-randomized design. The analyzed sample is 149 people (p. 5, §3.2; p. 24, Table 6), and cosine similarity is computed across participants’ actual essay outputs (pp. 7–8, §3.5.2; p. 26, Tables 10–11). Under the short-screen instructions, unclear assignment plus at least 50 analyzed people and an output-scored outcome gives core = unclear and referral to the two-screener pipeline.

one_line_finding: Among 149 analyzed participants with unstated condition allocation, the AI Values arm had lower between-writer essay similarity than No Intervention (M = 0.462 vs 0.531; p < .0001), without a significant increase in within-essay lexical diversity (PDF p. 5, §3.2; p. 10, §4.3; p. 26, Tables 10–11).
